habit_scope: IRC R602.10 / ABTG RR 1601-01 Method WSP or CS-WSP on 1–2 story wood SFR. Habit nailing 6 in edge / 12 in field. CS-PF portal is a VARIANT inside this method, not MF shear and not engineered hold-down walls. Glencoe 8d@3 is NOT this habit (D1).
how_it_is_done: This is the bracing that goes on stick (or 24 OC) walls — not a competing wall-raise. Designate BWLs (generally all exteriors). Parallel spacing tabulated to 60 ft (wind) or add an interior BWL / engineer (ABTG §1–2).

Place BWPs: <=25 ft OC along a BWL; start <=12.5 ft from each end. Typical min length 48 in (partial credit to 36 in with reduced contributing length). CS-WSP allows narrower panels (min length depends on adjacent opening height). Interior partitions are NOT credited for bracing (ABTG).

Pick method per BWL: intermittent Method WSP, or continuously sheathed CS-WSP when openings are many / narrow garage piers (ABTG §2.3; APA). Mix methods BWL-to-BWL; mixed types on one BWL use the conservative required length; do NOT mix sheathing types on one continuously sheathed BWL (ABTG).

WSP nailing HABIT is 6 in edge / 12 in field (IRC WSP; APA Table 22; Next-Gen Table 12). 3/8 in WSP @ 16 in studs: 6d common (2 x 0.113) 6/12. 7/16 in WSP @ 24 in studs: 8d common (2.5 x 0.131) 6/12. Fasteners 3/8 in from panel edges (APA). Wind/exposure caps: 3/8 in limited to 110/B, 90/C, 85/D (ABTG). Do NOT use Glencoe 8d@3 or APA Table 23 4/3/2 as this habit (D1).

APA: 1/8 in gaps at edges/ends; do not glue wall sheathing (buckling). ABTG: adhesive on BWPs not permitted SDC C/D. Block unsupported edges at bracing locations. Horizontal joints: block unless the segment is not a BWP, or provided bracing >=2x required, or GB is horizontal, or vertical joint is on double studs with 2 rows 10d box @ 10 in OC (ABTG).
CS-WSP generally no hold-downs; 24 in corner panels or 800 lb option to relax an end-panel rule (ABTG). Do not put WFCM 160 mph / SDC D1 hold-downs on a low-wind IRC CS-WSP house (D5).

CS-PF portal VARIANT (opening-friendly IRC path, not MF shear): as narrow as 16 in without hold-downs. Min 3x11-1/4 header SCL/glulam; 16 in–18 ft; h<=10; <=4 per BWL. 1,000-lb header straps (doubled in Exp C/D); portal grid nailing per IRC figure (APA Fig 11; ABTG Figs 7–8, 16). File here, not as m-P08-engineered-shear.

Sole plate at BWPs: 3-16d box (3-1/2 x 0.135) @ 16 in OC to joists/blocking, or 1/2 in anchors to foundation (ABTG §2.4 / R602.3(1)). Whole-plate carpentry (ch16 16d @ 16 in staggered) still applies off the BWP; follow the stricter BWP schedule on designated braced panels.

Uplift path at exterior BWPs supporting roof: Table R602.3(1) if <=90 mph Exp B, pitch >=5:12, span <=32 ft OR net uplift <=100 plf; else approved uplift connectors. AWC 160-mph example uses 1-1/4 in x 20 ga strap every stud, 4-8d each end — high-hazard EXAMPLE, not Wasatch/Fontana habit (D5).

Interior 1/2 in GWB is ASSUMED in WSP/CS-WSP bracing lengths (D6). If omitted, increase bracing length (ABTG Table 8 factor 1.4). Confirm with AHJ / engineer. Plans show BWLs, methods, BWP locations/lengths, and foundation top/bottom of BWPs.

when_this_beats_habit: This is the IRC habit bracing. CS-WSP/CS-PF beat intermittent WSP when openings eat the 48 in panels (narrow garage piers). Engineered shear is the alt when the house leaves the IRC box.
when_this_is_a_bad_idea: Feeding Glencoe 8d@3 or Table 23 4/3/2 into an IRC BWL house (D1). Putting WFCM 160 mph hold-downs on a mild-climate CS-WSP house (D5). Mixing sheathing types on one CS BWL. Crediting interior partitions. Treating CS-PF as MF podium shear.
why_tier1_never_learned_it: They sheathe. What they skip is BWL layout math, 6/12 vs 8d@3, and that CS-PF is an IRC portal not an engineered shearwall.
permit_gate: should be on drawings before permit
permit_gate_notes: BWLs and methods on drawings before permit. Engineer if spacing/end/corner rules fail or house leaves the IRC box. Confirm with AHJ / engineer.
risk_if_swapped_late: Switching WSP intermittent to CS-WSP/CS-PF after permit changes panel layout, corner returns, and portal headers. Switching to engineered shear is a PE path (m-P08-engineered-shear).
plain_language_summary: The code habit for holding the house sideways is a braced wall line with wood panels nailed 6 on the edges and 12 in the field. Three-eighths panels on 16-inch studs take 6d common; 7/16 on 24-inch studs take 8d common. Nails 3/8 inch in from the panel edge. Usually no hold-downs. Narrow garage piers can be a CS-PF portal down to 16 inches with a big SCL header — still IRC, not a podium shearwall. Do not nail 8d every 3 inches and call it bracing.
spanish_summary: El habito del codigo para el viento/sismo es linea de pared arriostrada con paneles clavados 6 en el borde y 12 en el campo. 3/8 en postes a 16 lleva 6d common; 7/16 a 24 lleva 8d common. Clavos a 3/8 de pulgada del borde. Casi nunca hold-downs. Un portal CS-PF puede bajar a 16 pulgadas con dintel SCL — sigue siendo IRC, no muro de corte de ingeniero. No clave 8d cada 3 pulgadas y lo llame riostra.
